message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-09-04 05:10 IST to 2026-09-05 05:10 IST (2026-09-03 23:40 UTC to 2026-09-04 23:40 UTC)

This scan used only `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt`. Entries were combined, obvious naming variants were normalized, duplicates were removed, and administrative/project-only rows were excluded. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

Two newly reported developments plausibly relevant to the primary inventory were verified. The actively exploited Chrome issue is the highest priority.

### Finding 1: Actively exploited Google Chrome V8 type confusion

- **Affected product:** Google Chrome before 152.0.7977.82
- **Vulnerability:** CVE-2026-85046
- **Severity:** High, as rated by Google
- **Description:** A type-confusion flaw in Chrome's V8 engine can allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the browser sandbox through crafted web content. Google states that an exploit exists in the wild.
- **Why it is relevant:** Google Chrome is explicitly present in the monitored product inventory.
- **Sources:** [Google Chrome Stable Channel Update](https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/09/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_01882797386.html), [Canadian Centre for Cyber Security advisory](https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/google-security-advisory-av26-883)

### Finding 2: Cisco Nexus 9000 Silicon One remote code execution

- **Affected product:** Specific Cisco Nexus 9000 Series switches containing a Silicon One ASIC
- **Vulnerability:** CVE-2026-20212
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 3.1 score 9.8
- **Description:** A remote unauthenticated attacker can reach TCP ports 43210 or 43211 in the default Layer 3 VRF and send crafted input that executes as root; exploitation can also crash S1HAL and reload the device.
- **Why it is relevant:** Cisco Nexus is explicitly present in the monitored inventory. Only the specific Nexus 9000 product identifiers listed by Cisco are affected.
- **Freshness note:** Cisco's first-party advisory was published September 2, before this scan window, but a new SecurityWeek report was published September 4 inside the window. This item is included as newly surfaced reporting, not as a newly issued vendor advisory.
- **Sources:** [Cisco security advisory](https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-n9k-s1-rce-EH8dEtr), [SecurityWeek report](https://www.securityweek.com/cisco-patches-critical-rce-vulnerability-in-nexus-9000-switches/)

### Mandatory MongoDB ecosystem sweep

MongoDB Server (Community and Enterprise), mongod, mongos, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, mongosh, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm and App Services, official integrations, and major maintained libraries/services were checked. No credible MongoDB-related vulnerability was first reported or substantively updated inside this scan window.

A MongoDB-owned batch covering libmongocrypt, the C/C++/PHP drivers, BSON libraries, and MongoDB for Visual Studio Code was published around 15:30–17:03 UTC on September 3, before the 23:40 UTC cutoff, and was excluded as stale for this run. A CERT-In MongoDB note showed a September 4 page update, but the underlying CVEs and disclosure were months old and no substantive new security development was verified.

### Other exclusions

Fresh SonicWall Network Security Manager findings were excluded because Network Security Manager is a different product from the monitored SonicWall SMA 8200V. Fresh VMware Workstation/Fusion findings were excluded because those products do not match the inventoried VMware ESXi, vCenter, Tools, Aria Operations, Cloud Foundation, or Telco product lines.

### Closing

Immediate review is recommended for Chrome because exploitation is confirmed. Cisco Nexus owners should promptly verify whether any deployed Nexus 9000 switch uses one of the affected Silicon One product identifiers and apply Cisco's fixed release or documented temporary mitigation as appropriate.
